meta.name: Project 1 - Go-kart space frame (v0)
meta.status_note: Every number in this file is a STARTING GEOMETRY used to teach the workflow. None of it has been measured from the Onshape blueprint or from a real kart. Replace values with measured ones before any steel is cut.
meta.axis_convention: x = forward from front axle centreline (positive rearwards), y = lateral (0 = centreline, positive = right hand side of driver), z = up from ground
meta.author: GT-09 Racing
meta.last_reviewed: not yet reviewed by an adult/professional

stock.label: 25 x 25 x 2.0 mm mild steel square tube
stock.use: Main rails. Thickest wall because these carry everything.

stock.label: 25 x 25 x 1.6 mm mild steel square tube
20 x 20 x 1.6 mm mild steel square tube
stock.use: Diagonal braces. Lighter because they only carry tension/compression along their length.

stock.label: 25 mm OD x 2.0 mm round tube

cutting.allowance_note: 5 mm left on every cut so the end can be squared and cleaned up. Do not weld a piece shorter than its finished length.

members.name: Main rail, left
members.why: The spine. Carries the driver, the seat, the engine and every other member that joins to it.

members.name: Main rail, right
members.why: Mirror of RAIL-L. Must be identical in length and straight.

members.name: Front crossmember
members.why: Stops the two rails closing together at the nose. Carries the front bumper mount.

members.name: Steering crossmember
members.why: Carries the steering shaft bearing and the pedal box. Must be square to the rails or the steering will pull to one side.

members.name: Mid crossmember
members.why: Front seat mounting point and torsion stiffener under the driver.

members.name: Seat back crossmember
members.why: Rear seat mounting point. Takes the load of the driver being thrown backwards.

members.name: Engine front member
members.why: Front edge of the engine bay. Also the node the rear diagonals tie into.

members.name: Rear crossmember
members.why: Rear bumper mount and the strongest point for a tow/push handle.

members.name: Nose diagonal, left
members.why: Turns a floppy rectangle into a stiff triangle at the nose, where steering loads enter the frame.

members.name: Mid diagonal 1, left
members.why: Forms a K-brace in the side bay so the frame resists twisting when one wheel hits a bump.

members.name: Mid diagonal 2, left
members.why: Completes the K-brace. Two short diagonals are stiffer than one long one.

members.name: Rear diagonal 1, left
members.why: Triangulates the engine bay. Engine torque tries to twist the frame; these members resist it.

members.name: Rear diagonal 2, left
members.why: Ties the rear crossmember into the engine bay node.

members.name: Steering shaft riser
members.why: Raises the steering shaft bearing above the frame so the wheel sits at chest height instead of lap height.

driver.note: Approximate proportions. LESSON 4 tells you how to measure your own body with a tape measure and replace these numbers.
